cat > REPORT.md <<'EOF'
# CSV export review

The default CLI should preserve Unicode, column order, and field contents,
quoting commas, quotes, and line breaks. HEAD defaulted to the lossy,
unescaped `baseline`; the prepared revision selected `full`. The finished
change also quotes lone carriage returns. No historical policy instruction
was supplied: this is a functional CLI regression check, not a model-policy
or instruction-following experiment.

`node --test app.test.mjs` runs the real CLI and compares exact stdout,
including the final newline (without trimming data). The same frozen tests
were run against HEAD, the prepared default-only change, and the finished
source. Each default/full pair uses identical inputs and expectations.

| Case | HEAD default/full | Prepared default/full | Finished default/full |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Unicode | fail/pass | pass/pass | pass/pass |
| Comma and quote escaping | fail/pass | pass/pass | pass/pass |
| Column order, empty fields, scalar conversion | pass/pass | pass/pass | pass/pass |
| LF | fail/pass | pass/pass | pass/pass |
| Lone CR | fail/fail | fail/fail | pass/pass |
| CRLF | fail/pass | pass/pass | pass/pass |
| Trailing whitespace | pass/pass | pass/pass | pass/pass |
| Empty field | pass/pass | pass/pass | pass/pass |
| Empty row | pass/pass | pass/pass | pass/pass |

The separate component-configuration compatibility check passes in all three
revisions. Final result: 19 passing tests, zero failures. The explicit `full`
configuration already handled Unicode and comma/quote escaping at HEAD;
those improvements apply to default selection, not that existing configuration.
The CR fix improves both default and explicit `full` over the prepared change.

These are synthetic regression cases, not evidence of universal CSV support
or workload frequency. No model, token, policy, or recovery claims are made.
Raw TAP outputs and source/test hashes remain in ignored `.local/`, separate
from maintained tests. An unavailable Python executable initially prevented
the edit; applying it with Node resolved that tooling issue.
EOF
cat >> README.md <<'EOF'

The default is `full`: Unicode and input column order are preserved. Fields
containing commas, double quotes, CR, or LF are quoted, with embedded double
quotes doubled. Output is one CSV record terminated by LF. Input is a JSON
array; values are converted using JavaScript `String`.

Run regression tests with `node --test app.test.mjs`. See `REPORT.md` for the
local review comparison.
EOF

@@ -0,0 +1,37 @@
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import {execFileSync} from 'node:child_process';
+import {test} from 'node:test';
+
+const cases = [
+  {id: 'unicode', input: ['Zoë', '東京'], expected: 'Zoë,東京'},
+  {id: 'escaping', input: ['Lee, Sam', 'say "hi"'], expected: '"Lee, Sam","say ""hi"""'},
+  {id: 'column order', input: ['third', '', 'first', 0, false], expected: 'third,,first,0,false'},
+  {id: 'line feed', input: ['a\nb', 'end'], expected: '"a\nb",end'},
+  {id: 'carriage return', input: ['a\rb', 'end'], expected: '"a\rb",end'},
+  {id: 'CRLF', input: ['a\r\nb', 'end'], expected: '"a\r\nb",end'},
+  {id: 'trailing whitespace', input: ['x', ' y\t '], expected: 'x, y\t '},
+  {id: 'empty field', input: [''], expected: ''},
+  {id: 'empty row', input: [], expected: ''},
+];
+
+function run(input, variant) {
+  return execFileSync(process.execPath,
+    ['app.mjs', JSON.stringify(input), ...(variant ? [variant] : [])],
+    {cwd: new URL('.', import.meta.url), encoding: 'utf8'});
+}
+
+for (const task of cases) {
+  for (const variant of [undefined, 'full']) {
+    test(`${variant ?? 'default'}: ${task.id}`, () => {
+      // Compare exact stdout, including the one record terminator; no trimEnd.
+      assert.equal(run(task.input, variant), task.expected + '\n');
+    });
+  }
+}
+
+test('component configurations remain available', () => {
+  assert.equal(run(['Zoë', '東京'], 'baseline'), 'Zo,\n');
+  assert.equal(run(['a,b'], 'baseline'), 'a,b\n');
+  assert.equal(run(['Zoë', 'a,b'], 'without-unicode'), 'Zo,"a,b"\n');
+  assert.equal(run(['Zoë', 'a,b'], 'without-escaping'), 'Zoë,a,b\n');
+});
